Brief approval and publication clearance remain pending.\n\n## Strategic assignment\n\n**Audience:** Venue owners with established reviews and ad creative who keep recycling the same message across discovery and retargeting.\n\n**Objective:** Help owners map a message to the question a couple needs answered at that stage.\n\n**Funnel & pillar:** Warm · Lightbulb Moments · Buyer psychology\n\n**Reader promise:** Know how to give discovery and consideration messages different jobs, and choose a review that answers a real buyer concern.\n\n**Belief shift:** From “a good testimonial should lead every ad” to “choose the message that helps this audience make its next decision.”\n\n**What makes this angle distinct:** This teaches message relevance across the couple’s decision journey. Ask what a couple needs to understand when they first discover the venue.\n2. Show a specific experience they can picture themselves in.\n3. Introduce a relevant review when it answers a remaining concern about choosing the venue.\n4. Map discovery, consideration, and inquiry messages; test the placement rather than assume one opening suits everyone.\n\n## Narrative framework\n\n**Hook:** Begin with a venue using an excellent testimonial repeatedly and ask what a newly discovering couple still needs to understand.\n\n**Problem:** Changing the photograph can leave the underlying message unchanged. Praise the existing proof while exposing the unanswered question.\n\n**Main point:** Let discovery messaging make the experience and fit concrete. Use relevant proof wherever it addresses a meaningful concern; placement remains a test.\n\n**Transformation:** Each message now helps the couple make a next decision rather than hearing the same general praise again.\n\n**CTA:** Ask which question a couple needs answered before booking a venue tour.\n\n## Evidence boundaries\n\n### What the meetings establish\n\n- The Meta review discussed underused venue angles and proposed moving experience-oriented and testimonial copy between funnel stages.\n- The account was still receiving leads during that discussion.\n\n### Proposed interpretations and tests\n\n- Experience-oriented discovery messaging and more relevant proof for warmer audiences may answer different questions.\n- The proposed placement needs testing; the export contains no post-change results.\n\n### Claims this brief does not support\n\n- Testimonials never work with cold audiences.\n- Moving the copy improved CPL or bookings.\n- The account was failing, or a particular buyer stage has one universally correct message.\n\n## Founder voice\n\n**Perspective:** Whitney as a thoughtful wedding-business strategist. Use “our team discussed” for a team member’s observation; use “I noticed” only for Whitney’s own recorded contribution. Describe the proposed refinement without claiming it has been launched or won. Use a fictional venue for copy demonstrations.\n\n**Outline:**\n\n1. Acknowledge that a strong review is valuable proof.\n2. Ask what the couple knows when they first discover the venue and what they still need to imagine.\n3.
